question: Which imaging test uses a strong magnetic field instead of X-rays to picture soft tissues?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Cerebral angiography
options.C: Plain skull X-ray
options.D: Computed tomography scan

explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radio waves to create detailed pictures without using X-rays.

question: What does it mean when a hormone comes from an 'ectopic' source?

options.A: An infection inside the anterior pituitary gland
options.B: An autoimmune reaction destroying thyroid receptors
options.C: A tumor outside the normal endocrine system that makes hormones
options.D: A complete failure of the hypothalamus to signal organs

explanation: Ectopic just means 'out of place'! It happens when abnormal tissues or cancer cells outside the usual glands start making hormones on their own. You're building great clinical knowledge. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the single best way to stop germs from spreading when handling specimens?

options.A: Changing the patient room air filters daily
options.B: Wearing two pairs of sterile gloves at all times
options.C: Spraying the examination table with bleach
options.D: Proper hand hygiene before and after the procedure

explanation: Simple handwashing remains your greatest superpower in infection control. Wash your hands religiously!

question: What happens when a patient internalizes societal HIV stigma?

options.A: They experience intense self-blame and shame
options.B: They immediately disclose their status to everyone
options.C: Their CD4 cell count automatically rises
options.D: They stop experiencing any physical symptoms

explanation: Internalized stigma causes patients to direct society's harsh judgments inward, leading to deep shame and self-blame. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of providing regular supportive supervision visits to rural community midwives?

options.A: To increase the paperwork burden without providing clinical assistance
options.B: To offer mentorship, solve operational challenges, and reduce professional isolation
options.C: To look for minor errors so the midwife can be publicly punished
options.D: To replace the midwife with an administrative clerk from the city

explanation: Supportive supervision focuses on guidance, problem-solving, and emotional encouragement rather than fault-finding, keeping rural health workers motivated. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h8)

question: Why do we use an incinerator (high heat) for body parts and tissues?

options.A: It operates at room temperature without requiring any fuel source.
options.B: It completely destroys anatomical material down to ash at very high heat.
options.C: It turns body tissues into recyclable plastic polymers for industry.
options.D: It is the only method that does not produce any smoke or gas emissions.

explanation: Incineration uses extreme heat to safely and completely turn anatomical waste into ash, which is important for health and safety reasons.

question: How do diuretic medications help bring down high blood pressure?

options.A: By helping the kidneys remove excess sodium and water
options.B: By blocking calcium entry into arterial wall cells
options.C: By strengthening the pumping force of the left ventricle
options.D: By directly slowing down the electrical conduction of the heart

explanation: Diuretics are 'water pills'! They tell the kidneys to flush out extra salt and water, shrinking the total fluid volume in the pipes so pressure drops.

question: Where do raw vegetables usually pick up dirt and bacterial spores?

options.A: From the chemical fertilizers sprayed on leaves
options.B: Directly from the soil during harvesting
options.C: Through the packaging materials used in transport
options.D: By absorbing them from the surrounding air

explanation: Correct! Because root crops and veggies grow right in the earth, contact with soil is the number one way they pick up environmental germs.

question: Where do endocrine glands release their hormones directly?

options.A: Extracellular tissue spaces
options.B: The lymphatic vessels only
options.C: Ducts leading to the skin
options.D: The bloodstream

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems. They pour their chemical messengers straight into the blood so they can travel all over the body!

question: Why do doctors perform a simple surgery called a hymenotomy for an imperforate hymen?

options.A: To create an opening in the membrane so trapped menstrual blood can drain
options.B: To treat an active bacterial vaginosis infection
options.C: To completely remove the entire vaginal canal
options.D: To reinforce weakened fascia against a developing cystocele

explanation: Spot on! Making a tiny cut in the blocked hymen relieves the pressure and lets the stored menstrual fluid empty out safely.

question: When a patient eats a heavy protein meal, which hormone is released to trigger heavy acid and enzyme production?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Gastrin

explanation: Gastrin is the signal booster! When protein arrives and stretches the stomach, gastrin is released to tell the stomach to produce more acid for digestion.

question: A diabetic patient is stressed because they cannot afford their monthly insulin. Who should the nurse involve first?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Surgical specialist
options.C: Social worker
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: Brilliant! Social workers are absolute rockstars at connecting patients with financial aid and community assistance programs.

question: You are getting ready to put a new colostomy bag on a patient. What is the right first step for the skin?

options.A: Rub a thick layer of oily moisturizing lotion to soften the skin
options.B: Scrub the area hard with an alcohol-based antiseptic
options.C: Dust the moist skin heavily with a scented powder
options.D: Clean the skin gently with warm water and pat it completely dry

explanation: Correct! The skin needs to be clean and totally dry so the adhesive barrier can stick securely without leaking.

question: Why do communicable diseases spread so quickly in crowded IDP camps?

options.A: Close living quarters and poor sanitation facilities
options.B: Frequent distribution of expired food supplies
options.C: Lack of available traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Mandatory daily group physical exercise routines

explanation: When people live very close together without proper toilets or clean water, infections spread easily from person to person.

question: On the AVPU neurological scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?

options.A: Voice
options.B: Ventilation
options.C: Vomiting
options.D: Vascular

explanation: Remember AVPU: Alert, Voice-responsive, Pain-responsive, and Unresponsive. It's a quick and handy way to check mental status!

question: What is the common underlying problem in chronic brain diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's?

options.A: Acute bacterial infection inside the ventricular system
options.B: Complete destruction of the skull bone structure
options.C: Abnormal folding and accumulation of specific proteins
options.D: Sudden rupture of major cerebral aneurysms

explanation: In these conditions, certain proteins misfold and clump together into sticky clusters that slowly harm brain cells over time.

question: A patient comes in with ringworm on their arm. What type of germ causes this common skin condition?

options.A: Fungi
options.B: Parasite
options.C: Bacteria
options.D: Virus

explanation: Correct! Don't let the name fool you—ringworm is caused by a fungus, not an actual worm. It loves warm, damp skin spots!

question: Which group of vitamins needs dietary fat to be properly absorbed by the body?

options.A: Water-soluble B-complex vitamins
options.B: Trace mineral cofactors
options.C: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
options.D: Ascorbic acid and related compounds

explanation: Correct! Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fats, so you need some dietary fat to absorb them into your bloodstream.

question: Which of the following is NOT a necessary step when receiving new stock on the ward?

options.A: Verifying that the expiration dates on the products are acceptable
options.B: Checking the physical items against the quantities on the delivery note
options.C: Hiding the delivery notes so other staff members cannot read them
options.D: Inspecting the packaging for any signs of damage or leakage

explanation: Delivery notes are official records that should be kept accessible for audits, not hidden away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why is observing a client in their home better than only seeing them in a clinic?

options.A: It reveals daily coping habits and environmental triggers
options.B: It replaces the need for any future medical doctor consultations
options.C: It removes all symptoms of mental illness permanently
options.D: It guarantees the client will take all their prescribed drugs

explanation: Being in the home gives nurses a realistic view of daily life, family stress, and living conditions that a clinic setting hides. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which imaging test is best for checking a suspected torn knee ligament?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.B: Standard skeletal X-ray
options.C: Computed tomography scan
options.D: Traditional bone scan

explanation: MRI uses strong magnets to create super clear pictures of soft tissues like cartilage and ligaments, making it the top choice for soft tissue knee injuries.

question: A conscious patient's random blood sugar is 52 mg/dL and they feel shaky. What should you do right away?

options.A: Give 15 grams of fast-acting oral carbohydrates
options.B: Send the patient for an emergency CT scan of the head
options.C: Inject long-acting insulin into the deltoid muscle
options.D: Wait patiently for two hours and test the blood again

explanation: Since the patient is awake and able to swallow, give them quick-acting sugar (like glucose tablets or juice) to bring their blood sugar back up safely.

question: What is the fastest and preferred energy source for your brain and nerves?

options.A: Glucose from carbohydrates
options.B: Fatty acids from dietary lipids
options.C: Amino acids from proteins
options.D: Vitamins from fresh fruit

explanation: Think of carbohydrates as premium fuel! They quickly break down into glucose, which is the brain's absolute favorite energy source.

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why local women rarely attend hypertension screening camps. What is the best initial action?

options.A: Close the screening camp and open a men's health clinic
options.B: Report the community to the ministry of health immediately
options.C: Assume women do not care about their heart health
options.D: Hold focus groups with local women to discuss their barriers

explanation: Engaging directly with the affected population through focus groups uncovers the real reasons behind low attendance. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h7)

question: In cervical cell changes, what makes CIN 3 more serious than the earlier stages?

options.A: The viral infection has completely cleared from the body
options.B: Dysplastic cells are confined strictly to the basal cell layer
options.C: Invasion through the basement membrane has already occurred
options.D: Severe dysplasia spans almost the entire thickness of the epithelium

explanation: You're learning fast! CIN 3 means the abnormal (dysplastic) changes have spread across almost the whole thickness of the surface tissue. The good news at this stage is that it hasn't broken through the basement membrane yet.

question: Why is the circulating nurse considered the patient's voice in the theatre?

options.A: Because the patient is unconscious and unable to speak for themselves
options.B: Because this nurse holds the legal license to perform surgery
options.C: Because this nurse decides what type of anaesthesia to give
options.D: Because this nurse stays inside the sterile zone at all times

explanation: Since the patient is asleep under anaesthesia, the circulating nurse acts as their advocate, watching out for their safety and comfort the whole time.

question: Why is it a big mistake to make someone vomit after they swallow a corrosive chemical (like strong acid)?

options.A: It always causes permanent paralysis of the vocal cords
options.B: It forces the poison directly into the urinary bladder
options.C: It neutralizes all antidote medications given later in the hospital
options.D: It can cause additional severe burns to the esophagus as the chemical comes back up

explanation: Brilliant thinking! Corrosive chemicals burn on the way down, and forcing them back up means they burn the throat a second time.

question: What is the medical term for a deep bone infection that can happen if a bite goes all the way down to the bone?

options.A: Cellulitis
options.B: Tenosynovitis
options.C: Fasciitis
options.D: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteomyelitis means an infection has reached the bone and bone marrow. It's a serious complication we try to prevent with prompt wound care and antibiotics.

question: A patient who just had major vulval surgery is crying and refuses to look at her wound. What is your best first response?

options.A: Contact the surgeon to prescribe a strong antipsychotic medication
options.B: Provide a compassionate, listening ear and validate her feelings
options.C: Tell her that the scars are completely normal and she should be happy
options.D: Force her to look at the wound immediately to speed up acceptance

explanation: Spot on! Changes to intimate body parts cause deep emotional pain. Sitting down to listen and validate her feelings builds vital trust.

question: Which of these is NOT a part of Evidence-Based Practice?

options.A: Respecting the unique values and choices of patients
options.B: Following strict historical traditions without question
options.C: Using clinical expertise to guide nursing actions
options.D: Critically appraising current research studies

explanation: Spot on! Evidence-based practice encourages us to question 'we've always done it this way' and instead rely on solid science and critical thinking.

question: Why are abstinence-only education programs often insufficient for protecting teenagers?

options.A: They force schools to close down health clinics
options.B: They cause physical delays in the maturation of the prefrontal cortex
options.C: They encourage teenagers to read explicit material online instead
options.D: They fail to give youth who become active the practical skills needed to prevent diseases and pregnancies

explanation: While abstinence is important, withholding practical information about contraception leaves sexually active teens completely unprotected. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: What is the primary function of lymph nodes?

options.A: Filtering lymph and trapping foreign invaders
options.B: Producing new red blood cells
options.C: Pumping lymph fluid through the body
options.D: Storing excess dietary fats

explanation: Lymph nodes act as filters that catch bacteria, viruses, and debris before fluid returns to the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: A pregnant woman having severe pre-eclampsia seizures is most likely to be given which mineral drug?

options.A: Atropine drops
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Ferrous sulfate
options.D: Quinine tablets

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is a vital mineral medication given via IV to stop and prevent dangerous seizures in pre-eclampsia.

question: A nurse wants to understand why mothers in a village refuse to bring children for immunization. Which method is most suitable?

options.A: Focus group discussion with mothers
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccine vials
options.C: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of infants
options.D: Counting the number of houses in the ward

explanation: Group discussions allow community members to freely share cultural beliefs, fears, and reasons behind specific health behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do doctors give antibiotics along with fluids when treating cholera?

options.A: To completely replace the need for drinking water
options.B: To rebuild the muscular lining of the stomach
options.C: To shorten illness duration and reduce bacteria shedding
options.D: To prevent the spread of mosquito vectors

explanation: Antibiotics aren't the main fix (fluids are!), but they help clear the bacteria faster so the patient recovers sooner.

question: What is closed-loop communication in a clinical setting?

options.A: Talking only through written memos left in a locked box
options.B: The receiver repeats the instruction back to confirm understanding
options.C: Using encrypted messaging apps for all doctor handovers
options.D: Restricting conversations to the nurse's station only

explanation: Closed-loop communication stops dangerous mistakes by ensuring the sender hears the exact message echoed back accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h4)

question: What is the main job of myosin light chain kinase (MLCK)?

options.A: To pump calcium back into storage sites
options.B: To break down ATP for cellular energy
options.C: To connect adjacent muscle fibers together
options.D: To phosphorylate myosin heads so they can bind to actin

explanation: Think of MLCK as the activator: it adds a chemical tag (phosphate) to the myosin head so it knows it's go-time and can grab onto actin!

question: Which environmental factor damages routine medicines the fastest?

options.A: Low room lighting levels
options.B: Clean wooden shelving
options.C: Quiet background noise
options.D: Excessive heat and moisture

explanation: Heat and humidity are tough on drugs—they break down chemical bonds and can render medications completely ineffective. Always keep them cool and dry!

question: Which historic international conference officially launched the modern concept of Primary Health Care (PHC) back in 1978?

options.A: The Abuja Health Summit
options.B: The Geneva Health Accord
options.C: The London Nursing Conference
options.D: The Alma-Ata Declaration

explanation: Spot on! The 1978 conference in Alma-Ata set the global standard for making basic health services accessible to everyone right in their communities.

question: An increasing population of older adults in Nigeria will most likely lead to a higher demand for what service?

options.A: Management of chronic health conditions
options.B: Primary school infrastructure
options.C: Pediatric immunizations and infant care
options.D: Obstetric and maternity wards

explanation: Older populations experience higher rates of long-term illnesses like high blood pressure and diabetes, increasing the need for chronic care. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of performing a pleurodesis via the intrapleural route?

options.A: To dissolve blood clots located inside the heart chambers
options.B: To deliver systemic antibiotics for a urinary infection
options.C: To obliterate the pleural space and prevent fluid return
options.D: To permanently dilate the main bronchial airways

explanation: Well done! Pleurodesis creates a controlled scar that seals the pleural space shut, stopping stubborn fluid or air from coming back.

question: Why do physical signs of puberty usually show up long after the internal hormonal changes have already started?

options.A: Because the skin blocks hormones from reaching the rest of the body early on
options.B: Because bones refuse to lengthen until a person turns twelve years old
options.C: Because internal chemical signals must build up and stimulate target organs over time
options.D: Because children eat too many processed foods before growing up

explanation: Well done! Hormones start working quietly behind the scenes in the brain way before you can actually see any physical changes on the outside.

question: What is an important joint protection tip you should teach patients to prevent deformities?

options.A: Use larger, stronger joints for lifting and carrying objects
options.B: Wear heavy splints continuously without removing them
options.C: Avoid all movement and stay in bed during flare-ups
options.D: Use smaller finger joints to lift heavy household items

explanation: Smart mechanics! For example, carrying a bag over the forearm instead of gripping it with the fingers protects small hand joints from extra strain and deformity.

question: A nurse uses a blood pressure cuff that is far too small for an adult patient with a large arm. What kind of reading is most likely to result?

options.A: A falsely low blood pressure reading
options.B: A reading showing zero systolic pressure
options.C: A falsely high blood pressure reading
options.D: A completely normal and accurate reading

explanation: Using a cuff that is too small requires excessive pressure to occlude the branch artery, leading to an artificially inflated blood pressure measurement. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h3)

question: While you are sliding an NG tube down, the patient suddenly coughs hard and turns a bit blue. What should you do immediately?

options.A: Listen with a stethoscope over the epigastric area
options.B: Immediately withdraw the tube into the pharynx
options.C: Encourage the patient to drink more water quickly
options.D: Push the tube in faster to get past the vocal cords

explanation: Coughing and turning bluish means the tube has wandered into the windpipe instead of the food pipe. Pull it back right away to let them breathe easily again!

question: Which of these is a core duty for a nurse managing a high-risk labour?

options.A: Coordinating care between specialists and providing bedside support
options.B: Prescribing restricted pharmaceutical drugs without doctor approval
options.C: Deciding the final legal outcome of any surgical procedures
options.D: Manufacturing the medical equipment used in the delivery suite

explanation: You are the heartbeat of the ward! Nurses bring everyone together—doctors, specialists, the mum, and her family—while offering loving bedside care.

question: Where do most traditional drug administration abbreviations come from?

options.A: Ancient Greek literature
options.B: Latin terminology
options.C: Modern medical shorthand
options.D: French pharmaceutical guides

explanation: Great job! Most medical abbreviations are rooted in old Latin terms that doctors and pharmacists used historically to describe how drugs should be taken.

question: A patient takes a bitter drug. Which family of receptors on their tongue will most likely detect that bitterness?

options.A: Acid-sensing ion channels
options.B: T1R family proteins
options.C: T2R family proteins
options.D: ENaC channels

explanation: Our mouth uses a specific family of proteins called T2Rs to sniff out and react to bitter plant alkaloids and medicines.

question: Why is the middle part (midpiece) of a sperm packed with mitochondria?

options.A: To store extra genetic material for embryonic development after fertilization
options.B: To generate the ATP energy needed to power the flagellum for swimming
options.C: To synthesize testosterone required for maintaining sperm motility
options.D: To produce protective enzymes that neutralize the acidic vaginal pH

explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell. The midpiece uses them to generate the energy (ATP) the tail needs to whip back and forth so the sperm can swim.

question: A patient with a new tracheostomy needs airway suctioning. Why is this considered skilled care?

options.A: It is a basic personal hygiene task that any family member can perform.
options.B: It replaces the need for daily medication administration.
options.C: It is only performed once a year during an annual physical exam.
options.D: It requires specialized clinical knowledge to prevent airway occlusion and infection.

explanation: Keeping an airway clear takes specialized training and sharp monitoring to stop dangerous complications like breathing trouble. Excellent work!

question: How is adenomyosis different from a normal uterus?

options.A: Endometrial tissue grows inside the muscular myometrium wall
options.B: The inner lining sheds continuously without hormonal triggers
options.C: Benign fibrous tumors develop on the outer serosal surface
options.D: The entire uterus drops below the pelvic floor muscles

explanation: Think of adenomyosis as the inner lining tissue burrowing into the middle muscle layer of the uterus, making the organ swell and feel tender.

question: Why is helping survivors and widows learn a skill or earn money so important for their recovery?

options.A: It stops traditional leaders from practicing medicine in rural areas
options.B: It is required by international laws before a patient can leave the hospital
options.C: It prevents them from remaining trapped in abusive environments due to financial dependence
options.D: It ensures the hospital receives full financial compensation for medical services

explanation: Spot on! Financial independence gives survivors the freedom and strength to step away from unsafe situations and care for themselves and their children.

question: Why does the foetal circulatory system bypass the lungs?

options.A: The heart pumps too slowly to reach the chest
options.B: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not oxygenate blood yet
options.C: The lungs are too small to receive blood flow
options.D: Oxygen is only needed in the lower body

explanation: Foetal lungs are collapsed and non-functional for breathing, so blood is shunted away from them toward the placenta. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h1)

question: Why do doctors order cardiac enzyme blood tests for a patient with severe chest pain?

options.A: To measure how fast red blood cells are moving
options.B: To test the liver's ability to process fats
options.C: To find out if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if heart muscle tissue has been injured

explanation: When heart cells die from lack of oxygen, they release specific enzymes into the bloodstream, confirming a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following must always be included when documenting a critical finding in a patient chart?

options.A: The personal opinion of the nurse about the patient's family
options.B: The name of every nurse working in the hospital
options.C: The exact cost of the diagnostic tests ordered
options.D: The exact time the finding was reported to the doctor

explanation: Recording the time of notification is legally crucial to prove timely communication and action during a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is interactive training better than just handing out printed rulebooks to food handlers?

options.A: It guarantees that workers will pass a written government exam
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future workplace supervision
options.C: It helps workers understand the practical reasons behind safety habits
options.D: It ensures that workers spend less time working in the kitchen

explanation: Demonstrations connect dry rules to real-life risks, making it much easier for staff to actually change their habits. Awesome!

question: A patient with damaged salivary glands will most likely struggle with which early step of digestion?

options.A: Absorbing water from the digested food bolus
options.B: Producing insulin to control blood sugar levels
options.C: Releasing bile acids to break down dietary fats
options.D: Forming a moist bolus for easy swallowing

explanation: Without enough saliva, food stays dry and scratchy, making it really tough (and uncomfortable!) to form a smooth ball (bolus) and swallow safely.

question: What is the official paper form that Nigerian health workers use to report adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Blue Card Sheet
options.B: Yellow Form
options.C: Red Discharge Tag
options.D: Green Admission Book

explanation: Whenever you spot a nasty drug reaction in practice, grab the NAFDAC Yellow Form and report it!

question: What is the Hawthorne effect when observing staff nurses during audits?

options.A: A sudden spike in patient admissions during the rainy seasonal period
options.B: The mathematical formula used to calculate hospital bed occupancy rates
options.C: The rapid physical exhaustion nurses feel toward the end of a night shift
options.D: Staff changing their behavior temporarily because they know they are being watched

explanation: The Hawthorne effect reminds us that people naturally change how they work when they know someone is watching them closely.

question: Which type of measuring tape should a nurse avoid using when checking body circumferences?

options.A: Fiberglass tape marked in centimeters
options.B: Steel tape with a rigid housing case
options.C: Non-stretchable synthetic measuring tape
options.D: Cloth tape that can stretch over time

explanation: Correct! Cloth tapes stretch out with repeated use, which will give you wrong numbers. Always go for non-stretchable tapes for accurate results.

question: What is the highest possible score on a standard muscle strength testing scale?

options.A: Ten
options.B: One hundred
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

explanation: Muscle power is graded from 0 to 5. A score of 5 means the patient has normal strength and can push hard against your full resistance.

question: Administering post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to a recent survivor of sexual assault falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Secondary prevention involves immediate medical interventions after exposure to prevent long-term harm like disease transmission. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h4)

question: Which sign points to a MILD drug reaction rather than a severe one?

options.A: Itchy hives on the skin with normal breathing
options.B: A sudden drop in blood pressure and fainting
options.C: Swelling of the tongue and throat
options.D: Wheezing across both lungs

explanation: Mild reactions usually stay on the skin as simple itching or hives, leaving the airway and breathing completely safe.

question: What is the term for the surgical procedure to cut scar tissue during childbirth in women with infibulation?

options.A: Curettage
options.B: Defibulation
options.C: Clitoroplasty
options.D: Hysterectomy

explanation: Defibulation is the surgical opening of the fused labia to allow for normal childbirth and examination. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h4)

question: What must a nurse do immediately after wiping a medication vial rubber top with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Allow the alcohol to dry completely before piercing
options.B: Blow on the rubber top to dry it fast
options.C: Insert the needle immediately while it is wet
options.D: Rinse the top with sterile tap water

explanation: Giving the alcohol time to air dry ensures proper disinfection of the rubber stopper surface. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h4)

question: A patient gets amoxicillin plus clavulanic acid for a tough infection. What does clavulanic acid do?

options.A: It acts as a mild sedative to help the patient rest
options.B: It increases urine production to flush out bacterial toxins
options.C: It blocks bacterial enzymes that normally destroy amoxicillin
options.D: It numbs local pain at the site of the infected tissue

explanation: Clavulanic acid is a trusty shield! It stops stubborn bacteria from producing enzymes that would normally chew up and destroy amoxicillin.

question: Why is it so helpful to know a patient's past surgical history?

options.A: It measures the patient's daily fluid intake and output
options.B: It provides the patient's current exact employment status
options.C: It replaces the need to ask about current prescription medications
options.D: It reveals previous reactions to anesthesia and surgical recovery issues

explanation: Spot on! Past surgeries let us know if they ever had trouble with anesthesia or healing, which keeps them safe today.

question: What is the primary goal of patient drug counselling in nursing practice?

options.A: Ensuring patient safety and therapeutic success
options.B: Shortening the daily doctor visit schedule
options.C: Fulfilling mandatory legal documentation quotas
options.D: Reducing the overall cost of hospital supplies

explanation: Counselling aims primarily to keep the patient safe from harm while helping the medicine work effectively. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of good nutrition for someone living with HIV?

options.A: To completely replace antiretroviral drugs
options.B: To support the immune system and enhance treatment
options.C: To prevent passing the virus to others
options.D: To guarantee permanent weight gain for everyone

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition gives your body the strength to fight off infections and helps HIV medications work much better.

question: What is the main danger of disconnecting the catheter tubing from the drainage bag?

options.A: It breaks the closed system and lets bacteria enter
options.B: It triggers severe allergic reactions to the plastic
options.C: It causes immediate permanent damage to the urethral sphincter
options.D: It creates high pressure that bursts the balloon

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the drainage system sealed and closed is the single best way to protect your patient from getting a catheter-associated infection.

question: Why does a patient with very high blood sugar (diabetes) end up with glucose in their urine?

options.A: The glomeruli are filtering extra protein instead
options.B: The distal tubule is secreting excess sugar
options.C: Water reabsorption in the loop has stopped completely
options.D: Renal transport carriers for glucose are overwhelmed
